hero.title: PCSSII Robotics
hero.body: PCSS II Robotics is a 501(c)(3) non-profit that aims to provide students with the opportunity to develop their technological skills and compete globally, without being limited by their resources or circumstances.

sections.title: A robotics community that turns curiosity into competition-grade capability.
sections.body: Students learn engineering, fabrication, coding, and leadership through real build cycles, competition culture, and community service. The program is designed to create confident makers who can solve problems under pressure.

pages.title: About the Team
pages.summary: PCSS II Robotics is a student-centered STEM program at Pioneer Charter School of Science II in Saugus, Massachusetts.

sections.title: We make engineering feel reachable.
sections.body: The team is built around a simple belief: students learn deepest when they are trusted with meaningful work. Robotics combines math, science, writing, design, code, public speaking, and teamwork into one shared challenge.

items.title: Safety before speed
items.body: Every build decision starts with protecting people and equipment.

items.title: Gracious professionalism
items.body: We compete hard while helping other teams get stronger.

items.title: Document the work
items.body: Students record decisions so the next teammate can learn faster.

items.title: Everyone contributes
items.body: Mechanical, software, strategy, media, and outreach all matter.

sections.title: Mentorship constellation
sections.body: Our strongest projects come from mentor-student pairs where technical rigor, communication, and ownership grow together.

tracks.label: Mentors & teachers
tracks.title: Guides who raise the ceiling
tracks.body: Mentors coach decision quality, review design tradeoffs, and model professional engineering habits.

members.name: Dr. Aarti Raman
members.focus: Mentors autonomous architecture, safety reviews, and build-season decision frameworks.
members.bio: Former controls engineer who now helps students convert ambiguous ideas into measurable sprint plans.
members.quote: Great teams are not built on heroics. They are built on repeatable learning.

members.name: Ms. Leena Patel
members.focus: Leads fabrication readiness, tool safety, and community STEM workshops led by students.
members.bio: Connects classroom fundamentals with shop-floor confidence so new members can contribute quickly.
members.quote: Confidence appears when students can explain why a design works, not just that it works.

tracks.label: Students & team members
tracks.title: Builders who carry ownership
tracks.body: Student leaders run modules end-to-end and teach new teammates through documented playbooks.

members.name: Maya Chen
members.focus: Owns telemetry dashboards, autonomous testing loops, and code review rituals.
members.bio: Built a reusable troubleshooting board that reduced repeated pit-side software failures.
members.quote: The robot gets better when our notes are as good as our code.

members.name: Aditya Nair
members.focus: Leads drivetrain assembly, tolerance checks, and repair playbooks for events.
members.bio: Designed a modular service checklist now used across pre-match inspections.
members.quote: Reliable robots win because reliable teams communicate under pressure.

pages.title: Circuit 2026
pages.summary: Circuit is the latest hackathon being held by PCSSII Robotics. With a racing theme, attendees build projects over a 2-day period from 8AM to 8PM, competing for big-ticket prizes and learning skills along the way.

sections.title: Circuit • June 6-7, 2026
sections.body: Welcome to Circuit, a hackathon where speed and function are everything. Make a website, game, or hardware project, but once the time runs out, it's anyone's game. Let's race.
sections.note: The event runs from 8 AM to 8 PM over two days with racing-themed builds, workshops, and prizes.
highlights: Student-built websites, games, and hardware projects
Two-day build sprint with races and prizes
Held at Pioneer Charter School of Science II

sections.title: PCSS II Robotics presents its latest hackathon.
sections.body: Circuit is the latest hackathon being held by PCSSII Robotics. With a racing theme, attendees build projects over a 2-day period from 8AM to 8PM, competing for big-ticket prizes and learning skills along the way. It's being held at Pioneer Charter School of Science II from 8 AM to 8 PM from June 6th to June 7th.

sections.body: The event includes check-in, meals, workshops, mini games, working time, submissions, voting, and the closing ceremony.
